page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with running head and page number at the top. No margin notes, no notes below the text. Catchword "quod" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: his defudatum eft, non tamen ex omni parte absolutam esse obfervarunt viri doctiffimi, ita ut fortasse adhuc pumice critico indigeat: Cumque MS. habeamus verfionis 70 quod Alexandrinum vocamus, ex Bibliotheca Regia defumptum, ipfi Vaticano nec antiquitate, nec finceritate cedens, de cujus editione vir doctus Patricius Junius multis abhinc annis cogitavit, ejufque librum unicum Iobi fcil. Londini, fpeciminis ergo, promulgavit, unde magnam per orbem Chriftianum inter viros doctos expectationem de ejus editione excitavit: De hoc nobiliffimo & antiquiffimo monumento, quod Bibliis noftris adjiciendum duximus, aliquid breviter praefari libet. MS. hoc ex Alexandria fecum attulit Cyrillus Lucaris nuper Patriarcha Alexandrinus, cum ad fedem Patriarchalem Conftantinopolitanam promotus effet, tanquam magnum Orientis Thefaurum, illudque Regi noftro qui magnum librorum impreffórum fuppellectilem eidem Cyrillo misit, per D. Thomam Roe equitem auratum Regis apud Turcarum Imperatorem legatum, dono dedit, quod ut pretiofiffimum κειμήλιον[?] in Bibliotheca fua Regia asservari juffit. Scriptum vero erat (ut teftatur idem Cyrillus propria manu ad initium libri,) per S. Theclam prout fama erat apud Alexandrinos, ejufq; Theclæ nomen libro infcriptum erat, quod jam obliteratum non conspicitur: licet vero

page.notes: The first word is printed with a long s, read as "his"; the initial letter is uncertain. The Greek word κειμήλιον is printed in a worn form, and its letters are uncertain. The printed text ends at the bottom with "quod", which is the catchword. Show-through and page damage are not transcribed. Printed "impreffórum" has an accent-like mark; it is read as "impressorum" with [?] left off because the reading is clear enough.
